items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: By the time we got to the next place Willard Alexander’s office, the phone was off the hook.

ctx.x: “Three More Foxes,” “The Fox Hunt,” this and that. So I went with that band for a year. And man, when I got out of that band, I mean it was totally different than DeFranco’s band. This was a bunch of pirates. I mean these guys were half from England, and they didn’t care. I mean the bus used to just throb when it would go down, like we actually rolled a joint I think the length of the bus one time. It went from the front to the back. I mean each guy in the aisle is doing it like this and that. But when I got out…

some reason. I don’t remember exactly why. But then in the morning we came to pick it up. Well the English guys, one was — a couple of managers and sound guys and this and that, we brought the bus by to pick up the equipment and somebody said where’s so-and- so face (an expletive face) and the poor girl that was one of his students pointed into the band director’s room. We got our stuff. But these guys had gone through — these English roadies and managers had gone through that high school and placed smoke bombs…
